newsitem.title: FINLAND: Clinton hails tentative airline labor agreement.
newsitem.headline: Clinton hails tentative airline labor agreement.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Thursday hailed a tentative labor agreement between American Airlines and its pilots' union, saying labor management cooperation helps the United States compete more effectively in the global marketplace.

"I want to commend the management of American Airlines and the leadership of the Allied Pilots Association for their commitment to each other and to the travelling public," said Clinton, who added that it spoke well of the parties that the tentative agreement was reached more than five weeks before the end of a cooling off period he imposed after the pilots briefly struck the airline last month.

"When labor and management work together as they did here, U.S. industries are better able to maintain their prominent positions in the global marketplace," Clinton said in a statement issued in Helsinki, Finland, where he was holding a summit with Russian President Boris Yeltsin.

The tentative labor agreement between American Airlines and its pilots' union was to be presented to the union's board of directors for their approval on Friday and was subsequently to be submitted to the union membership for ratification. Union rank and file previously rejected a tentative contract, sparking the crisis that brought Clinton's intervention last month.

In his statement, Clinton thanked Robert Harris, the chairman of a presidential emergency board appointed to mediate the contract dispute. The President also thanked the two members of the panel, Helen Witt and Anthony Sinicropi, for their dedication and hard work.
"This settlement would not have been possible without their leadership and hard work," he said.
